headline: For normalized independent unit-interval banks and any rotated signature (1,1,-1), the entire positive one-sheet density is maximized at the cone tip; when the negative eigenvector is bank-aligned, the two-sheet side is also tip-dominated, so the latest first-order optimal account03/B17 cone-tip witness is globally tip-maximal.
mathematical_premises: Each normalized sum of independent unit-interval uniforms has an even log-concave density; products, orthogonal changes of variables and linear marginals preserve log-concavity, and central symmetry is preserved.
Pinned e5f71d79eff325201dd0274053d20268ce65b837 Theorem C gives the exact one-sheet ruling identity p(s)=(pi/sqrt(2)) avg_theta rho_theta(sqrt(s)e_theta) for signature (+,+,-).
A centrally symmetric log-concave marginal is maximized at zero, yielding p(s)<=p(0) for s>0 without any post-rotation independence premise.
For the aligned negative bank, the squared-bank density b(v)=g(sqrt(v))/sqrt(v) is decreasing, and independence of disjoint original banks gives p(-r)=int a(u)b(u+r)du<=p(0).
The physical synthesis frame R satisfies R^T R=I_3, hence RBR^T has exact nonzero spectrum {1,1,-1}.

partner_result_actually_applied.application: Partner's first-order cone-tip optimizer aligns the negative eigenvector with the smallest bank and uses continuous proportions sqrt(24):sqrt(57):sqrt(57). The new global-tip theorem upgrades its cone-tip expansion to the actual global density norm. The partner's second-order formula was also specialized exactly to the explicit 20q,20q,13q bank family.

exact_consequences: For integer allocations within O(1) of the optimal proportions, ||p_Q||_infinity = 3sqrt(2)[1-K_*/N+O(N^-2)], K_*=(sqrt(24)+2sqrt(57))^2/640=63/160+3sqrt(38)/80.
correction_scope: The proof uses neither uniform pointwise quadratic-phase decay nor a dimension-free fiber supremum, never asserts spectral-coordinate independence, and handles the aligned negative side by the actual disjoint-bank convolution rather than a generic two-sheet X-ray estimate.
unresolved_implication: For genuinely non-aligned rotations of the same three-bank uniform family, only the minority-sign/two-sheet side can still create an off-tip peak. Arbitrary rough non-log-concave bank laws and broader target geometries remain outside this theorem.
next_step: Attack the non-aligned two-sheet side using original bank-product structure, preferably by a monotonicity or rearrangement identity that does not invoke the refuted generic X-ray-only mechanism; alternatively construct a valid finite >3sqrt(2) peak in a genuinely non-CLT/shared-row geometry.
